positions.name: CalibrationVerifiedAgainstReferenceStandard
positions.frame: what makes the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration count as verified — the reference standard it is checked against?
positions.why: All three expressions perform the same directional move: they establish the spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration as settled specifically because it was checked against the June reference plates — src-1 makes this move in prose ('verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds'), while src-2 and src-3 restate the identical fact in labelled-field form ('**Calibration**: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates'). The relational read (authority-ranking: the reference plates hold the rank the instrument must match) and the value read (competence, appealed to through the verification act) both track this same alignment-to-standard logic across all three, and the register read confirms they share one flat technical delivery — so this is one directional read genuinely spanning three expressions, not three independent claims.
